title: Ex-Fatah Official Abu Zaida: Israel and Hamas Were Close to a Deal Before October 7
detail: Sofian Abu Zaida, the former senior Fatah official who last week identified himself as 'Coal Eyes' — the mediator who passed Yahya Sinwar's pre-attack 'earthquake' warning toward Israel via an adviser to the UAE president — said Monday, September 21, 2026 that Israel and Hamas had been close to signing an agreement before the October 7, 2023 massacre. Abu Zaida said the negotiations, which he described as separate from and not a cause of the eventual attack, centered on releasing four Israeli hostages held since earlier incidents in exchange for Palestinian prisoners and an easing of Gaza's blockade. He offered few additional specifics on how close the sides came or why the talks collapsed, but the disclosure adds to his account of serving as a back-channel between Sinwar and Israeli officials in the weeks before the assault.

media.caption: Sofian Abu Zaida says Israel and Hamas were close to an agreement before October 7, 2023

title: Analysts: Israelis Feel Less Safe Than Before October 7 Despite Military Gains Against Hamas, Hezbollah, Iran
detail: An Al Jazeera analysis published Monday, September 21, 2026, ahead of the third October 7 anniversary and the October 27 election, canvassed Israeli and UK-based analysts on whether Israelis feel safer than on October 6, 2023. King's College London security analyst Ahron Bregman said an 'objective military assessment would indicate that, overall, Israel is safer' given that Hamas's capabilities have been reduced, Hezbollah weakened, the Assad government ousted in Syria, and Iran's military depleted — but warned he 'can see a third Palestinian Intifada on the horizon' that 'will be difficult to stop' once it starts. City St George's University political scientist Ayala Panievsky said Israelis nonetheless 'do not feel safe from future attacks by Hamas or Hezbollah, or a nuclear threat from Iran,' pointing to shattered public trust in Israel's security institutions after the October 7 failure. The piece noted the war has killed more than 73,000 Palestinians in Gaza by its count, and that security dominates the upcoming election's debate.

media.caption: Analysts weigh whether Israelis feel safer nearly three years after October 7, 2023
